evidence.snippet: [Issue #610](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/610) fixes the three acknowledge findings that the host round at 02d0ad4c raised on [pull request #576](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/576). The maintainer ruled on 2026-11-20, in the coordinator's session, that #576 lands first and these follow before the gate. Each fix starts from a test that fails at the head before it.

        severity: P3

verification.reason: Line 3 of the added progress-log file says "that #576 lands first". That `#576` follows a space and a space follows it, and it is not link text. The repository's own `bare-issue-reference` pattern, `(^|[\s(])#\d+([^\w\]-]|$)`, matches it. The rule's message cites the AGENTS.md instruction to link every issue and pull request mentioned. The earlier mention in the same sentence is linked, but the rule has no exemption for a repeated mention. The defect is real and advisory, and the claim is already at P3, so there is nothing to lower.

In #rests, a no-check lens record whose key the round reads satisfies early(), so extra() is true and it counts toward relayLimits.extras, whether or not the round names it. That is deliberate: the comment at line 217 says these records count "whether or not the round names them". The bound has two tests. One (line 281) uses unnamed triage records. The other (line 300) uses named triage records. Neither includes a named, no-check lens record. The early-copy tests at about 404–449 each add one unnamed copy, so they never approach the bound. A mutation that skips read lens records before the extra() test would pass all of them. I did not run the suite, but no test I read reaches that path.
